recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core FHIR follow-up is needed for FHIR-7307 unless Patient Administration intentionally reopens broader RelatedPerson demographic duplication policy.
issue_request: FHIR-7307 was a Published/Persuasive Patient Administration DSTU1 change request to add birthDate to RelatedPerson, analogous to Person, because the age of an individual involved in care may matter. The final resolution says to add the birthdate as a date, and a Jira comment asked to include it as a search parameter.
initial_application: Git commit a96f358a486ac632eadda2a5de834bc1a64e29f2, "Tracker# 7307 RelatedPerson to include birthDate", added RelatedPerson.birthDate as a 0..1 date element to the historical RelatedPerson spreadsheet. The 2021 source rework commit 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 migrated RelatedPerson into the current XML StructureDefinition and search-parameter bundle while retaining the applied change.
additional_context: RelatedPerson is active in source/fhir.ini as a current resource with PA approval status. Person.birthDate is also a date, so the current RelatedPerson datatype matches the final resolution rather than the issue summary's loose dateTime wording. Searches found no later final FHIR-core decision or direct Zulip/Confluence discussion that reverses the element or search parameter; FHIR-17504 is later no-change background about RelatedPerson demographics and does not alter this issue.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source files were edited because source/relatedperson/structuredefinition-RelatedPerson.xml already defines RelatedPerson.birthDate as 0..1 date, and source/relatedperson/bundle-RelatedPerson-search-params.xml already defines the RelatedPerson-birthdate date search parameter over RelatedPerson.birthDate.

related_jiras.note: Later Resolved - No Change RelatedPerson proposal discussed duplicated demographics and the role/person distinction, but did not remove or contradict RelatedPerson.birthDate.
